questions.question: In app/src/lib/qr.ts, does resolveScanDestination avoid every vacuous/placeholder path — specifically: (a) does the card branch genuinely call normaliseScanPayload -> parseContactCard (including real signature verification) rather than a shortcut that returns a destination without verifying the signature; (b) is the new group-invite validator's hex-join check and npubToPubkeyHex(admin) check live logic, not a stub that always returns true or a frozen test-only constant; (c) is there no tautological assertion in the accompanying tests (e.g. asserting typeof result === 'string' without asserting the exact string) that would pass unchanged if the branch body were replaced with `return null`?

Does resolveScanDestination stay entirely within the QR lib module (app/src/lib/qr.ts) per architecture.md's Boundary Rules — no import of router, window, or any Navigation UI / Scanner UI module; does the card branch delegate to the existing normaliseScanPayload/parseContactCard seam rather than duplicating parse/verify logic (DD2); and is the group-invite validator placed beside normaliseScanPayload rather than introduced as a new top-level module or registry (per the Out-of-Scope 'no extensible link-registry' constraint)?

Could QR lib be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its dependencies_allowed list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md?

Does app/tests/unit/qr-scan-destination.test.ts (or wherever the tests land) provide unit/property coverage of resolveScanDestination across the full input space named in the stories.json seam contract and AC-ROUTE-1..6 — valid card (bare npub, nostr:-prefixed, https://.../add#c=... link, raw base64url payload), valid group invite, signature-failing card, group-invite missing each of join/admin/name individually, malformed admin/join, arbitrary text/URLs, empty string, and a non-few.chat-origin invite URL — and is the test suite an independent exercise of the exported function rather than a shadow-init that re-implements resolveScanDestination's body inside the test file?

Does the implementation match the epic's stated design decisions as a coherent whole — DD1 (route to the exact generator URL forms, no re-implementation of /add or /groups inbound resolution), DD2 (card branch reuses normaliseScanPayload/parseContactCard verbatim, no new card-parsing code), and DD3 (group-invite validation is new, minimal, pattern-based, and explicitly does not pin origin to few.chat) — with evidence drawn from the actual qr.ts diff, not from the story description alone?

Given resolveScanDestination parses attacker-controlled, camera-decoded external input as a URL and as hex/npub values, does the implementation handle every malformed variant defensively — no uncaught throw from `new URL(value)` on garbage input, no unbounded/ReDoS-prone regex applied to an arbitrary-length string, npubToPubkeyHex decode failures caught and treated as null rather than propagating an exception — and is there a test asserting resolveScanDestination never throws for any string input (per the seam contract's 'never throws' invariant), evidenced by an actual fuzz-style or malformed-input test case, not just a docstring claim?

For every value form AC-ROUTE-1 names (bare npub, nostr:-prefixed npub, https://few.chat/add#c=<payload> link, raw base64url card payload) that parseContactCard accepts, does resolveScanDestination return the exact `/add#c=<payload>` deep-link form? Show the production branch that produces this string and the test(s) that exercise each named value form end-to-end (not a single representative case standing in for all four), and confirm the test is not a mock-spy proxy over parseContactCard.

For a well-formed group-invite URL (pathname is the /groups/ invite path, valid hex join nonce, admin decodes via npubToPubkeyHex, non-empty name), does resolveScanDestination return the exact `/groups?join=…&admin=…&name=…` string with all three parameters preserved verbatim from the input? Show the production code performing this construction and the test asserting the exact returned string (field-by-field), not merely that a non-null value was returned.

Does a card value whose signature fails verification return null from resolveScanDestination, with no downgraded/bare-pubkey fallback path? Show the production code path proving verification failure short-circuits to null (not to a partial destination), and a test that constructs a value with a deliberately invalid signature and asserts strict null.

Does resolveScanDestination return null for a group-invite-shaped URL missing join, admin, or name (each tested individually), for an admin that is not a valid npub, and for a join that is not a well-formed nonce? Show the validator logic performing each check and one test per missing/malformed parameter (not a single combined case), confirming no partial-match acceptance.

Does resolveScanDestination return null for plain text, a random https:// URL unrelated to few.chat, an empty string, and a /groups/ URL with no invite params? Show the fallback path producing null for each and the corresponding test cases, confirming none of these inputs accidentally satisfies the card or invite branch.

Does the group-invite branch accept a well-formed invite URL built from a non-few.chat origin (e.g. few-chat.pages.dev or a localhost dev origin) with identical acceptance behavior to a few.chat-origin URL, proving no origin comparison gates acceptance? Show the validator code confirming origin is never read/compared, and a test using an explicitly non-few.chat origin that still resolves successfully.

Does the ScanDestination seam contract (stories.json#seams[0]) hold in full against the shipped resolveScanDestination — exact return-string shape for both branches ('/add#c=<payload>' and '/groups?join=<hex>&admin=<npub>&name=<name>'), the function's synchronous/pure/DOM-free signature (no router, no window, no network access anywhere in its call graph), and the 'never throws for any string input' invariant — verified by inspecting the actual exported function signature and call graph, not only by reading the story description? This is the seam S2 consumes without further verification of its shape; a gap here propagates undetected into S2.

app/src/lib/qr.ts's normaliseScanPayload (existing, unmodified) returns the trimmed/nostr:-stripped INPUT itself, not an extracted payload — for a full https://.../add#c=<payload> link input it returns the whole link string, not just <payload>. resolveScanDestination therefore layers a new local helper, extractCardLinkPayload (qr.ts:86), which finds the '#c=' marker and slices the trailing substring before it is embedded in the '/add#c=' destination. Does the shipped code actually call extractCardLinkPayload on every card-branch return (qr.ts:154), and is there a regression test proving the full-link input form does NOT get double-wrapped (i.e. resolveScanDestination(buildShareUrl(payload)) !== '/add#c=https://few.chat/add#c=' + payload)? A naive implementation that embedded normaliseScanPayload's return value directly would silently double-wrap the full-link case while still passing the bare-npub and raw-payload cases — is that specific failure mode covered?

parseGroupInviteUrl (qr.ts:116) requires url.pathname to be EXACTLY '/groups/' (GROUP_INVITE_PATHNAME, qr.ts:96) — the trailing-slash form buildInviteUrl (marmot/inviteLinkGeneration.ts) always produces under this app's trailingSlash:true static-export config. Is this exact-match choice (rather than a trailing-slash-tolerant comparison) actually consistent with every real invite link the app itself ever generates, and does the test suite cover the boundary case of a '/groups' (no trailing slash) URL to confirm it is correctly rejected rather than silently accepted or silently mis-routed? Confirm this isn't an unverified assumption about a URL library's normalization behavter (e.g. does the WHATWG URL parser silently add/remove the trailing slash for some inputs before .pathname is read).

INVITE_JOIN_NONCE_PATTERN (qr.ts:102-103) hardcodes an exact 32-hex-character length, matching generateNonce()'s current 16-byte output (marmot/inviteLinkGeneration.ts, out of this story's scope to modify). This is an implicit cross-module contract enforced only by this regex, with no shared constant or import binding the two. Is this coupling documented clearly enough (code comment at qr.ts:99-101) that a future change to generateNonce()'s byte length would be caught by a human reading this file, given the group-invite validator is explicitly scoped as 'minimal, pattern-based' rather than importing the generator (DD3)? Is this an acceptable, deliberate scope boundary rather than a latent bug?
